• ArchitecturalDecision — "Frameworks excluded from value refs"
  hasDescription: Frameworks are not a separate value-reference coverage axis; value refs are framework-agnostic and framework behavior belongs to route-node extraction. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#1 §2b says the README framework list is a separate route-node extraction feature, value-refs cover constants through underlying language support, and no separate framework matrix is needed.

• Lesson — "InitSync options are ignored"
  hasDescription: Do not rely on `CodeGraph.initSync(dir, opts)` include options during value-ref validation: `initSync` takes only the path and default config indexes `.ts`, `.tsx`, and `.js`. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#3 §7 lists this as a trap already hit.
  hasAuthor: codegraph docs <bootstrap>

• ArchitecturalDecision — "Inherited template value refs"
  hasDescription: Svelte, Vue, and Astro value-reference coverage is inherited through their existing script/frontmatter reparse path rather than implemented as separate language work. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#1 §2b says their extractors re-parse `<script>` or frontmatter as TypeScript/JavaScript in `VALUE_REF_LANGS`, verified that `.svelte` consts edge readers, and no separate matrix row is needed.

• Consequence — "Fifteen-language value-ref validation"
  hasDescription: The shipped value-reference feature passed the documented validation matrix across all fifteen supported languages: TS/JS, Go, Python, Rust, Ruby, C, Java, C#, PHP, Scala, Kotlin, Swift, Dart, and Pascal kept node counts identical on/off, held precision guards, and showed that disabling value refs makes impact analysis under-report constants read by many symbols. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges.md#1 Validation matrix states node count never moved across S/M/L repos in all fifteen languages, precision guards held, and the `impact` OFF column is the bug.
  hasAuthor: codegraph docs <bootstrap>
  hasLifecycleStatus: accepted
  resultsFrom: https://moosedev.dev/kg/ArchitecturalDecision/90ef68e1-06f6-4691-8b80-a73ad30afb83

  hasTimestamp: 2026-06-16T17:16:00Z
  https://moosedev.dev/kg/Consequence/c6bbcc58-b090-478d-af24-302f6169a3ce

• Lesson — "Parse fidelity before C++ value refs"
  hasDescription: Do not retry C++ value-reference edges until parse fidelity is solved, because partial guards against ERROR ancestors and compound-statement declarations still leave class-member, parameter, template, macro, and header misparse leaks. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#0 §2 says DON'T retry C++ without solving parse fidelity first and lists the residual leak classes.
  hasAuthor: codegraph docs <bootstrap>
  hasLifecycleStatus: accepted
  learnedFrom: https://moosedev.dev/kg/ArchitecturalDecision/2a680f48-6a0b-4fc8-ab44-8aea62544c9e
  hasTitle: Parse fidelity before C++ value refs
  hasTimestamp: 2026-06-16T17:16:00Z
  https://moosedev.dev/kg/Lesson/8ee9c602-cfce-4b8d-a45b-9789c04c6585

• Lesson — "Value-ref agents need impact calls"
  hasDescription: Value-reference edges do not reduce agent reads unless the agent calls an edge-traversing tool such as `impact` or `explore`; the durable win is blast-radius correctness exposed through `getImpactRadius`. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges.md#3 Agent A/B says indexed-repo runs used one codegraph call with 0 Read/0 Grep in both arms, often called `codegraph_search`/`callers` instead of `impact`/`explore`, and explicitly says not to claim value-refs reduce agent reads.
  hasAuthor: codegraph docs <bootstrap>
  hasLifecycleStatus: accepted
  learnedFrom: https://moosedev.dev/kg/ArchitecturalDecision/8a2d2161-956f-4866-8898-ba1a5a9346a9
  hasTitle: Value-ref agents need impact calls
  hasTimestamp: 2026-06-16T17:16:00Z
  https://moosedev.dev/kg/Lesson/0044433c-d193-4c34-a550-668f33c02047

• Constraint — "Value-ref PR workflow"
  linkedVia: isConstrainedBy
  hasDescription: Value-reference validation and precision work must follow the documented PR hygiene: branch from main, keep pure validation docs/test changes separate from focused precision code fixes when practical, put user-facing changelog entries under Unreleased, include the specified generated-by trailers, and leave merge decisions to the maintainer.
